ruling.recommended_action: Close the fare dispute as no overcharge (fixed RydeX quote unaffected by the drive), record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file, and send the account to Ryde for review of the repeated route deviation (RD-6).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a completed RydeX fixed-quote ride: the rider was billed 10.7 km / $24.93, which equals the quoted optimal distance, and billed distance did not exceed the optimal route [F4][F6]. Because RydeX is a non-metered service, the extra 4.5 km driven [F1] never entered the fare, so RD-2's metered branch (extra_km × distance_fare ÷ distance_km) yields nothing to refund; only an unpublished or unmet surcharge item could be refunded, and the bill contains only base, distance, time, platform fee, with waiting $0.00 and no toll item [F6][RD-2][FARE-1]. The refund portion of the claim therefore fails on the numbers, and the amount is nil.

The off-route segment 14:19–14:26 (5.03 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.39 km, +3.64 km, up to 1160 m off route) is nonetheless a real unexplained deviation, and RD-1 sets no percentage or kilometre threshold — any unexplained off-route stretch breaches the shortest-and-most-direct obligation [F1][F3][RD-1]. I checked each excuse. RD-4 does not apply: there is no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch and the speed-band records for AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY and CENTRAL EXPRESSWAY are only band 4 (30–39 km/h), i.e. not band 1 or 2, and a band record cannot exempt a segment on its own [F9][F10][F11][RD-4].

For RD-5, there is no rider consent at all: the in-app chat is empty, so nothing was sent by the rider before 14:19:10, and the driver's after-the-fact statement ("The GPS rerouted me, that's all") is a claim, not consent [F7][F8][RD-5]. A complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment means the segment counts, so I find F3 "counts". RD-3 likewise gives no exemption — no rider-named place and no measured stop appears in the record [F7][RD-3].

That finding changes no money (fixed fare) but it does decide the account action: a non-exempt segment means the driver is in breach of RD-1, and the driver profile shows 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, i.e. this is a repeated route breach, which calls for flagging the account for review [F14][RD-6]. The rider also asked for the detour to be "on record", which this ruling does.

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the (empty) chat and the driver's statement — there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation anywhere, so the finding is "none" [F7][F8][SAFE-1]. Evidence is sufficient: the fare records, the GPS segment, the complete chat record and the traffic records settle every element this ruling needs [F3][F4][F6][F7][F11].
